name: Saint Martin I
dates: Died 655 · Rome, Constantinople and the Crimea
history: A pope who defended the truth that Christ has a human will as well as a divine one, against the policy of the Emperor. Arrested in Rome, tried in Constantinople and exiled to the Crimea, he died there of hunger and ill-treatment in 655. He is the last pope honoured as a martyr.
life: Martin, born at Todi in Umbria, was a deacon of Rome and the pope’s representative at Constantinople before his election in 649. The Emperor had forbidden all debate on whether Christ had one will or two, hoping to silence a dispute that divided the East. Within months of his election Martin held a synod at the Lateran, with Saint Maximus the Confessor’s support, which taught that Christ, true God and true man, has both a divine and a human will, and condemned the imperial decree. In 653 the Emperor Constans II had him seized in the Lateran, sick in bed, and shipped to Constantinople. There he was imprisoned, tried for treason, publicly stripped and condemned to death, a sentence changed to exile at Cherson in the Crimea. His letters from exile speak of hunger and of feeling forgotten. He died there in 655.
prayerTo: Saint Martin, you would not trade the truth about Christ for the favour of an emperor. Pray for the Pope and for all who suffer for the faith in prison or exile. When I feel forgotten, help me to trust that God forgets no one, and to stay faithful to the end. Amen.
penance: Martin died hungry and forsaken. Eat simply today and give the difference to a charity for prisoners or refugees, and pray for the Holy Father.
meditation: Hungry and forgotten in exile, he still commended his Church to God. Whom do you find it hardest to pray for?
